Record a timestamped track

Record a GPX track on iPhone or Apple Watch.

Apple Watch users do not need to export a GPX file. LensPin reads recorded workout routes directly from Apple Health via read-only HealthKit access. Choose a workout route in LensPin; no Strava sync or Health export is needed. A GPX file is a route file containing times and coordinates, useful for other recorders or when you prefer a file.

For a separate GPX file, one workflow is to start an outdoor activity before the first camera photo, keep it running through the outing, and export the saved recording as GPX afterward.

Choose for export convenience, not workout metrics.

Plans, prices, and menu names can change. The links below lead to each developer’s current documentation.

Option 1 · Strava on iPhone

Optional: export a GPX file.

  1. Open Strava and tap RecordChoose an outdoor activity such as walk, hike, run, or ride. Allow precise location and Motion & Fitness access when prompted.
  2. Wait for the location indicator outdoorsBegin before taking the first camera photo. For a clearer photo timeline, leave auto-pause off when practical and let the recorder cover stops as well as movement.
  3. Finish and save the activityKeep the activity private if you do not want the trip visible to other Strava users. Wait for the upload to complete.
  4. Open the activity on strava.comStrava currently provides file export on its website. Open the activity’s More menu and choose Export GPX.
  5. Move the file to the iPhone if neededUse iCloud Drive, AirDrop, or the Files app, then select that .gpx file in LensPin.

Option 2 · Direct export and offline maps

Keep the track closer to the device.

OSMAND

Record with Trip Recording

Start the Trip Recording tool, finish and save the track, then open My Places → Tracks. On iOS, Export or Share sends the selected track as a GPX file through the system share sheet.

Official recording guide ↗Official export guide ↗
GAIA GPS

Record, save, then export

Start a track from the map’s Record control. After the trip, open Saved, select the recorded track, tap Share, choose Export File, and select GPX.

Official recording overview ↗Official iOS export guide ↗
GURU MAPS

Record a GPS track

Start a recording in Guru Maps, finish it after the last photo, then open the track details. Use the export action at the bottom of the details screen and save the track to Files.

Official GPS tracks guide ↗
TEST FIRST

Run a five-minute rehearsal

Whichever app you choose, record a short walk, export it, and confirm that LensPin sees timed track points before relying on it for a full trip.

Apple Watch

Three dependable export paths.

1. Record directly with Strava on Apple Watch

Install the Strava watch app, authorize Health and Motion & Fitness access, choose an outdoor sport, and save the activity. When it syncs to Strava, export GPX from the activity page on strava.com.

Official Apple Watch instructions ↗
2. Record with Apple’s Workout app, then sync to Strava

In Strava, connect Health and allow Workouts & Routes. Strava can import eligible native Apple Workout activities from the previous 30 days; after the activity appears, use Strava’s website export.

Official Apple Health sync instructions ↗
3. Record and export with WorkOutDoors

WorkOutDoors records outdoor workouts on Apple Watch and supports GPX export in its iPhone companion app. It is a useful option when you want watch maps and a direct file workflow.

Official WorkOutDoors user guide ↗
Apple Health’s full export is not a ready-to-import GPX file.

You do not need Apple Health’s full export for LensPin: select the recorded workout route directly. Use a GPX export only if you want a separate file.
